name: Mihomo
summary: A configuration-driven proxy client and tunnel that separates TCP/UDP ingress dispatch from protocol-specific outbound adapters, provider-backed proxy groups, and controller/configuration concerns.

features.name: TCP/UDP tunnel dispatch boundary
features.description: Mihomo exposes a tunnel boundary that accepts TCP connections and UDP packets, initializes bounded worker queues, tracks NAT and session state, and dispatches traffic through configured proxy adapters. This is the local data plane, not a remote control plane.
benefits: Provides one data-plane path for transparent, local, and proxy-routed traffic
Bounds UDP work queues and hashes packet sessions to workers
costs: Queue overflow can drop packets under load
NAT, DNS mode, sniffing, and process lookup add state to connection dispatch

features.name: Adapters, providers, and selectable proxy groups
features.description: Outbound proxy adapters share a common dial/UDP/resolution interface. Provider-backed groups materialize, filter, cache, health-test, and select adapters; a selector forwards traffic through the currently selected member.
benefits: Adds many protocol clients behind one outbound adapter boundary
Separates remote proxy membership/provider refresh from per-connection dialing
Supports explicit selection and health-oriented groups
costs: Protocol-specific adapters still differ in UDP, DNS, and transport capabilities
Provider refresh and health checks introduce mutable shared group state
Selection and fallback semantics can change the path for subsequent connections

features.name: Configuration-driven local control boundary
features.description: The configuration executor parses local configuration and initializes DNS, proxy, rule, and tunnel state. Mihomo may expose controller APIs through its hub surface, but the reviewed source separates those management routes from the adapter/tunnel packet path; no external control-plane authority is assumed by this card.
benefits: Makes runtime composition explicit through configuration and initialization stages
Keeps controller/configuration concerns separate from common adapter dialing interfaces
costs: Configuration reloads must coordinate registries and live traffic
Controller/API availability is separate from proxy data-plane availability

mathematical_views.question: How do inbound TCP/UDP traffic, tunnel workers, proxy adapters, groups, and providers form the local forwarding graph?
assumptions: Tunnel, adapters, groups, and providers are distinct vertices
A provider/group edge represents membership or refresh, while a tunnel/adapter edge represents traffic dispatch
Controller APIs and external subscription services are outside the packet forwarding graph

mathematical_views.question: How are TCP and UDP ingress events admitted, queued, assigned to workers, and dropped when capacity is exhausted?
assumptions: UDP queues have finite capacity and packet hashing selects a worker queue
TCP and UDP paths have different lifecycle and NAT/session behavior
The model does not infer fairness or throughput from queue sizes

mathematical_views.question: How does a configured provider-backed group move from member materialization to selection, health testing, fallback, and dialing?
assumptions: Provider versions and cached proxy lists represent refreshable state
A selected proxy is an adapter implementing the common outbound contract
Health-test results influence group state but do not prove end-to-end availability

costs: Queue overflow can drop packets under load
